name: Independence Pass · CO 82
description: 36 miles of Colorado Highway 82 between Aspen and Twin Lakes, crossing the Continental Divide at 12,095 ft — the highest paved state highway in Colorado. Narrow, with sections that have no centerline and no guardrail.

sources.title: Aspen Chamber: Everything you need to know about Independence Pass

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags this route between 25 and 55 mph depending on the section (town streets in Aspen vs. open highway), but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: Closed every winter — typically mid-to-late November through late May — with gates at Lincoln Creek Road on the west side and Graham Gulch on the east. CDOT also bans any vehicle (or vehicle-plus-trailer combination) over 35 ft at any time, year-round, due to the narrow, winding road. Both are firm rules, not general caution.

name: Million Dollar Highway · US 550
description: 23 miles of US 550 between Ouray and Silverton over Red Mountain Pass (11,018 ft), part of the San Juan Skyway. Narrow, with sharp switchbacks, steep drop-offs and long stretches with no guardrail.

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Red Mountain Pass has real, recurring closure history: permanent avalanche-control equipment was installed after years of active winter avalanche mitigation, and the road has also closed for rockfall (November 2024) and flood/debris removal (July 2026). Check current conditions before relying on this being open.

name: Trail Ridge Road · US 34
description: 47 miles of US 34 across Rocky Mountain National Park between Estes Park and Grand Lake, reaching 12,183 ft — the highest continuous paved road in North America. Wide sweeping curves above treeline rather than tight switchbacks.

sources.title: NPS: Trail Ridge Road and Old Fall River Road opening and closing dates

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Closed every winter, typically late October through Memorial Day weekend — the exact dates depend on snowfall and are announced each year, not fixed. A National Park entrance fee applies. This is inside Rocky Mountain National Park, not open backcountry highway.

name: Lizard Head Pass · CO 145
description: 24 miles of CO 145 between Telluride and Rico over Lizard Head Pass (10,222 ft), the western leg of the San Juan Skyway. Sweeping mountain curves through the San Juan National Forest.

sources.title: Wikipedia: San Juan Skyway Scenic and Historic Byway

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Check current Colorado road conditions before a winter trip; mountain sections can ice over and this pass sees real snowfall.

name: Lookout Mountain Road
description: The Lariat Loop's switchback climb from Golden up Lookout Mountain, about 6 miles with a gentle-by-comparison 5% average grade but a steady sequence of hairpins. One of the most popular close-to-Denver climbs, shared heavily with road cyclists.

sources.title: Visit Golden: Lookout Mountain Mile-by-Mile Guide

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Heavily used by road cyclists year-round, including as a training climb for professional races; expect to share the full width of the road on weekends and mornings.

name: Mount Blue Sky Road · CO 5
description: Colorado Highway 5, formerly Mount Evans Road — the highest paved road in North America, reaching 14,130 ft. Narrow with hairpin turns and no guardrails on the upper section between Echo Lake and the summit.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway
CDOT: Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans)

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Closed for a multi-year improvement project through 2025; scheduled to reopen for the 2026 season around Memorial Day weekend, timed entry and a reservation required in season. This is a seasonal high-altitude road, not a year-round route — check current status and the reservation system before a trip.

name: Deer Creek Canyon Road
description: A foothills canyon road between Chatfield Reservoir and Evergreen, about 9.5 miles of sweeping and sharp turns following the creek up into the mountains. A long-standing local favorite for motorcyclists and sports car drivers.

sources.title: The Gazette: Cycling Colorado — Deer Creek Canyon

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Pavement is generally decent but carries loose gravel in spots; weekends bring meaningfully heavier traffic than weekdays.
